facebook.post: On this week's Buzzcut episode with Shakeel Dalal, we talked about something you've probably noticed if you've been house-hunting in Longmont: those old prefab homes that were once considered cheap starter stock are now some of the most sought-after (and expensive) single-family houses in town. Shakeel breaks down the cycle: how homes built without footers or frills get incrementally improved by each generation of owners, evolving into the 'eclectic' neighborhoods we cherish today. Brady shares how his own Old Town house has been added onto and fixed up over nearly a century, transforming from bare-bones to something much more. It's a fascinating lens on why we can't just 'build like we used to,' because we never really did. Have you seen this play out in your own neighborhood, or in a house you've lived in?

Then energy prices spiked, everyone added gas, and now we're going full circle back to electrification. From this week's Buzzcut with Shakeel Dalal. Full episode link in bio.

facebook.post: On this week's Buzzcut episode with Shakeel Dalal, we learned that neighborhoods like Southmoor and the streets up around 21st and Grant were built in the late sixties and early seventies with zero gas hookups. All electric, all baseboard heating. You can still spot those homes by the lampposts out front with little light sensors on them. Energy prices made those homes expensive to heat, so families spent decades converting to gas stoves and pellet stoves. Now, fifty-some years later, Longmont is pushing electrification again. It's a funny full-circle moment. Do you live in one of those original all-electric homes, or remember when your family made the switch to gas?
